value.reason: The Evidence matches the positive pattern for SEC-14. terraform/networking.tf defines an aws_efs_file_system named "${var.project_name}-sqlite-data", so it holds the app's SQLite database. terraform/main.tf defines a Fargate ECS task definition for the same app. Through the Sequelize Address model (models/address.ts) and AddressModel.create in data/datacreator.ts, the database stores personal profile data tied to a UserId: full name, mobile number, street address, city, state, zip code and country. None of the supplied Terraform shows any backup control for this file system, such as an aws_backup_plan or aws_backup_selection targeting it, or an aws_efs_backup_policy. Encryption is also left to a variable (var.efs_encrypted) instead of being enforced. The negative example differs only by having that backup plan and selection. Without a backup, the Data Fiduciary has no way to keep processing this data if it is lost or becomes inaccessible, which Rule 6(1)(d) specifically requires. One caveat: the Terraform excerpts are cut off, so the volume mount and the absence of a backup resource elsewhere in the repo are inferred, not fully shown.
